report: The provider or checkpoint, the resolved revision, and the date that revision was confirmed.
The exact decoding temperature and any other sampling parameter active at evaluation time.
The literal question text, the option identifiers sent to the model, and the rubric bound to each identifier, kept as separate fields.
The smallest positive value the model can return, and the share of returned probabilities equal to zero.
How the state was serialized into the model input, the token budget, and any truncation rule.
Whether the reference label is human adjudicated, a single human rating, a crowd rating, a teacher model, a model consensus, or a synthetic procedure.
The item count, the grouping against near-duplicate leakage, and whether the set predates the cutoff.
Classwise calibration or a reliability diagram by class, reported beside any top-label accuracy value.
The ranked probability score, or the calibration of the cumulative probabilities at each ordinal threshold.
The Fréchet and Hoeffding interval or a stated dependence model, rather than the product of the marginals.
The exact confidence formula, the answer-set size it was computed on, and whether it was compared across sizes.
The screening stage forwarding rate and the downstream detection rate, reported as two separate values.
The routing threshold or band, the assumed costs of a false positive, a false negative and a review, and the resulting review volume.
Latency and cost with the hardware, the batch size and concurrency, and whether the value is a vendor claim or an independent measurement.
A stated rule for a mid-study change to a served checkpoint or a default parameter, including which rows are re-run.
Both the earlier and the later value when a revision change causes disagreement, each with its own revision, date and resolution.
